scenario.title: Atlas of Questions
scenario.premise: Follow records, arguments and instruments as they are translated, challenged and put to new work—then combine them into explicitly speculative future laboratories, shared memories and living cities. Historical chapters are dated teaching reconstructions, not an inevitable march toward truth; the future inventions are fiction, not forecasts.

stage.title: A sky worth recording
stage.speaker: Workshop keeper
stage.motivation: A cloudy night has left a gap. Make an account another scribe can check, then mark when to watch the Moon again.

result.label: Seen / clouded / missed
result.text: Watch 1: the event was seen. Watch 2: cloud hid the relevant part of the sky. Watch 3: no observer was present. “Not seen” has three different evidential meanings here.
result.attribution: Authored observational dossier, not a Babylonian quotation.

result.attribution: Historical paraphrase of the research scope in Rochberg; no ancient words quoted.

stage.title: What does a prediction prove?
stage.speaker: Workshop keeper
stage.motivation: Two speakers predict the same shadow but give different causes. Show what follows from each claim—and what the prediction cannot decide.

result.label: Every dimming = cover
result.text: Speaker A: “Every darkening is caused by a covering body. This is a darkening. Therefore a body is covering the light.” The observed case and the universal premise are different claims.
result.attribution: Fictional teaching speech, not Aristotle’s dialogue.
